prompt.en:
Write `causal_mask(n)` that returns an `n x n` NumPy float array to add to the attention scores before the softmax.

- Cell `(i, j)` is `0` when token `i` may look at token `j` (itself and the past, `j <= i`).
- Cell `(i, j)` is `-inf` for the future (`j > i`), so its weight after the softmax is exactly 0.
prompt.es:
Escribe `causal_mask(n)`, que devuelve un array float de NumPy de `n x n` para sumar a las puntuaciones de atención antes del softmax.

- La celda `(i, j)` vale `0` cuando el token `i` puede mirar al token `j` (a sí mismo y al pasado, `j <= i`).
- La celda `(i, j)` vale `-inf` para el futuro (`j > i`), de modo que su peso tras el softmax es exactamente 0.

tests:
import numpy as np
m = causal_mask(3)
assert m.shape == (3, 3), "the mask is n x n"
assert np.all(m[np.tril_indices(3)] == 0), "positions on and below the diagonal (self and past) must be 0"
assert np.all(np.isneginf(m[np.triu_indices(3, 1)])), "positions above the diagonal (the future) must be -inf"
assert np.allclose(np.exp(causal_mask(4))[0], [1, 0, 0, 0]), "after exp, the first token keeps weight only on itself"
assert causal_mask(1).tolist() == [[0.0]], "a single token sees only itself"

hint.en: `np.triu(np.ones((n, n)), k=1)` marks the future with ones. `np.where` can turn those into `-np.inf` and the rest into `0.0`.
hint.es: `np.triu(np.ones((n, n)), k=1)` marca el futuro con unos. `np.where` puede convertirlos en `-np.inf` y el resto en `0.0`.

prompt.en:
Write `attention(Q, K, V, causal=True)` for one head: `softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d_head) + mask) V`, where `d_head` is the width of `Q` and the mask is the causal mask when `causal` is true.

- The softmax runs over each row and must be numerically stable: subtract the row maximum before `exp`.
- Return an array with one row per query and the width of `V`.
prompt.es:
Escribe `attention(Q, K, V, causal=True)` para una cabeza: `softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d_head) + máscara) V`, donde `d_head` es el ancho de `Q` y la máscara es la causal cuando `causal` es verdadero.

- El softmax se aplica a cada fila y debe ser numéricamente estable: resta el máximo de la fila antes de `exp`.
- Devuelve un array con una fila por consulta y el ancho de `V`.

tests:
import numpy as np
Q = np.array([[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0], [1.0, 1.0]])
K = np.array([[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0], [1.0, 1.0]])
V = np.array([[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0], [5.0, 5.0]])
out = attention(Q, K, V, causal=True)
assert out.shape == (3, 2), "the output has one row per query and the width of V"
assert np.allclose(out[0], V[0]), "with the causal mask the first token can only attend to itself"
s = np.exp(np.array([0.0, 1.0]) / np.sqrt(2))
w = s / s.sum()
assert np.allclose(out[1], w[0] * V[0] + w[1] * V[1]), "row 2 must weight V[0] and V[1] by the softmax of scores divided by sqrt(d_head)"
full = attention(Q, K, V, causal=False)
assert full[0, 0] > 1.0, "without the mask the first token also sees V[2] = [5, 5]"
big = attention(np.array([[1000.0, 0.0]]), np.array([[1000.0, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0]]), np.array([[1.0], [2.0]]), causal=False)
assert np.all(np.isfinite(big)), "subtract the row maximum before exp so large scores do not overflow"

hint.en: Compute `scores = Q @ K.T / np.sqrt(Q.shape[1])`, add `np.triu(np.full((n, m), -np.inf), k=1)` when causal, subtract `scores.max(axis=1, keepdims=True)`, exponentiate and divide by the row sums.
hint.es: Calcula `scores = Q @ K.T / np.sqrt(Q.shape[1])`, suma `np.triu(np.full((n, m), -np.inf), k=1)` si es causal, resta `scores.max(axis=1, keepdims=True)`, aplica la exponencial y divide por la suma de cada fila.

solution:
import numpy as np


def attention(Q, K, V, causal=True):
    Q = np.asarray(Q, dtype=float)
    K = np.asarray(K, dtype=float)
    V = np.asarray(V, dtype=float)
    scores = Q @ K.T / np.sqrt(Q.shape[1])
    if causal:
        scores = scores + np.triu(np.full(scores.shape, -np.inf), k=1)
    scores = scores - scores.max(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    weights = np.exp(scores)
    weights = weights / weights.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    return weights @ V
